Draft answers below. I attached an updated diagram and a one-page attestation snapshot that we can share with the customer. Markus, please review the diagram annotations (I called out the mTLS boundaries and the admin bastion flows).

Short summary (TL;DR): The control plane is logically and network-segmented from inference data-plane instances. Control-plane components run in a customer-agnostic control VPC (or optionally in a customer-managed control plane for private deployments). Data-plane inference workers execute in dedicated tenant pools (either shared hardware with multi-tenancy controls or physically isolated pools for Dedicated/Private). All control → data-plane control signals traverse authenticated mTLS channels and are proxied through per-cluster sidecars to avoid direct inbound admin access.

Responses to SecureTrust questions:

1) Diagram / demarcation
- Attached: control-plane-diagram-v2.png (PNG) — shows three layers: public ingress, control plane, and tenant inference pools with explicit VPC/subnet references and peering.
- Separation: control plane components (scheduler, model registry, control API) live in a separate VPC/subnet group with network ACLs that only allow outbound control ports to inference pools. Tenant workloads are restricted to data-plane subnets; administrative interfaces for tenants are accessible only via a hardened bastion or our control-plane proxy. No management plane ports are open to the public internet.

2) HSM usage & attestation
- HSM providers supported: AWS CloudHSM (default for Redwood-hosted), Azure Dedicated HSM, and YubiHSM for on-prem/edge options.
- Key lifecycle: customer encryption keys (for tokenized secrets and customer-provided keys) can be generated in an HSM-backed key store via PKCS#11 or KMS API; private key material never leaves HSM.
- Rotation: default rotation schedule is 30 days for signing keys; data encryption keys are rotated per-tenant quarterly. Emergency rotation procedures exist (immediate rekey + one-hour model/instance restart window) and are logged.
- Attestation evidence: we surface HSM attestations as signed cert chains and appliance audit logs. The attached hsm-attestation-snapshot.pdf shows a sample attestation bundle (hardware cert, attestation timestamp, and digest) — we can provide live attestation on request for dedicated/private installs.

3) Brief threat-model summary (control-plane focus)
- Risk: compromised control-plane admin credential → potential unauthorized model deployment or control signal injection.
  Mitigations: RBAC with least privilege, session-based ephemeral admin tokens, mandatory MFA, signed deployment artifacts, and per-request attestation checks on model images.
- Risk: lateral movement from control-plane to tenant instances (privilege escalation).
  Mitigations: microsegmentation, egress/ingress ACLs, enforced mTLS with mutual cert rotation, sidecar proxy ACLs, and per-tenant encryption-at-rest keys.
- Risk: supply-chain/model-poisoning (malicious artifact uploads).
  Mitigations: artifact signing/verification, reproducible build/checksum verification, pre-deployment eval gating, and quarantine for unverified images.

Attachments included: control-plane-diagram-v2.png (image/png)
                   hsm-attestation-snapshot.pdf (application/pdf)

Let me know if you want the attestation in a different format (PKCS#7 bundle, HSM pubkey fingerprint, etc.). I recommend offering SecureTrust the PNG + PDF for the RFP packet and, if they require, a secured link to a Vault that shows live HSM attest logs (we can rotate credentials before sharing).
